newPages.title: Oblivious interactive hash function
newPages.definition: An interactive hash function with an obliviousness guarantee, introduced by Barnum and Heath, that can be constructed from a random oracle yet implies oblivious transfer via a non-black-box reduction.

newPages.title: Circular security
newPages.definition: The assumption that an encryption scheme remains secure when the adversary is given an encryption of the scheme's own secret key (a key cycle), which is not implied by standard IND-CPA security.

newPages.title: Falsifiable assumptions
newPages.definition: An assumption is falsifiable if a violation of it can be witnessed by a polynomial-time game between a challenger and an adversary, so that a counterexample can be efficiently recognized; KEA-style knowledge assumptions are not.

newPages.title: Functional encryption
newPages.definition: A public-key encryption scheme in which a master secret key issues functional keys $\sk_f$, and a holder of $\sk_f$ learns $f(m)$ from an encryption of $m$ and nothing more.

newPages.title: Shortest Vector Problem
newPages.definition: The promise problem of deciding, given a lattice basis and a parameter $d$, whether the lattice's shortest nonzero vector is shorter than $d$ or longer than $\gamma \cdot d$, for an approximation factor $\gamma$.

newPages.title: Ideal Shortest Vector Problem
newPages.definition: The Shortest Vector Problem restricted to ideal lattices -- lattices arising as ideals in the ring of integers of a number field -- which is the worst-case problem underlying Ring-LWE and Ring-SIS.

newPages.title: Learning subspace with noise
newPages.definition: For a uniformly random rank-$k$ secret matrix $\mathbf{C} \in \FF^{k \times n}$, the $(k,n,\mu)$-LSN assumption states that samples $\mathbf{a}_i^T\mathbf{C} + \mathbf{e}_i$ -- where each $\mathbf{e}_i$ is uniform in $\FF^n$ with probability $\mu$ and zero otherwise -- are computationally indistinguishable from uniform.
newPages.stripAliasFrom: content/References/CIMR25 - Secret-Key PIR from Random Linear Codes.md

newPages.title: One-way state generator
newPages.definition: A one-way state generator maps a classical key to a quantum state from which no efficient quantum adversary can recover a consistent key; it is the quantum analogue of a one-way function and may be strictly weaker.

newPages.title: Pseudorandom generator in $\mathrm{NC}^1$
newPages.definition: A pseudorandom generator whose output is computable by a logarithmic-depth boolean circuit family ($\mathrm{NC}^1$); its existence is one of the four hypotheses of the JLS21 iO construction.

newPages.title: $q$-Strong Diffie-Hellman assumption
newPages.definition: Given the power sequence $(g, g^\tau, g^{\tau^2}, \ldots, g^{\tau^q})$ in a bilinear group with secret $\tau$, no efficient adversary can output a pair $(c, g^{1/(\tau + c)})$ with $c \in \ZZ_p$.

newPages.title: Random Oracle Hypothesis
newPages.definition: The (refuted) conjecture, attributed to Bennett and Gill, that complexity-class relationships holding for almost all relativized worlds also hold unrelativized.

newPages.title: Rerandomizable encryption
newPages.definition: A public-key encryption scheme with a public rerandomization algorithm that maps any ciphertext to a fresh ciphertext of the same message, distributed as a fresh encryption of that message.

newPages.title: Shortest Independent Vectors Problem
newPages.definition: $\mathrm{SIVP}_\gamma$ asks, given a basis of an $n$-dimensional lattice, for $n$ linearly independent lattice vectors whose longest is within a factor $\gamma$ of the smallest achievable; it is one of the two worst-case lattice problems that LWE and SIS reduce from.

newPages.title: Module lattice problems
newPages.definition: The module analogues of the shortest-vector and shortest-independent-vectors problems, stated for lattices arising as modules over the ring of integers of a number field; Module-LWE and Module-SIS reduce from their worst-case hardness.

newPages.title: Anonymous credentials
newPages.definition: A credential system in which a user obtains a credential from an issuer and later proves possession of it, and of the attributes it certifies, without revealing her identity and without letting distinct showings be linked.

newPages.title: Authenticated encryption
newPages.definition: A symmetric-key encryption scheme that provides both message confidentiality and ciphertext integrity, so that decryption rejects every ciphertext not produced by a holder of the key.

newPages.title: Permuted puzzles assumption
newPages.definition: The assumption that a secretly permuted Reed-Muller code is indistinguishable from random -- equivalently, that moderate-degree polynomials are indistinguishable from random functions given permuted versions of their evaluation graphs -- introduced as the basis of the first SK-DEPIR candidate.

newPages.title: co-Computational Diffie-Hellman
newPages.definition: The CDH problem across the two groups of an asymmetric bilinear pairing: given $g_2, g_2^a \in \GG_2$ and $h \in \GG_1$, compute $h^a$; it is the assumption under which BLS signatures are EUF-CMA secure in the random oracle model.

newPages.title: Deniable encryption
newPages.definition: A public-key encryption scheme in which a sender who is forced to reveal both the message and the randomness used to encrypt it can instead produce convincing fake randomness explaining the ciphertext as an encryption of any alternative message.

newPages.title: Distributed key generation
newPages.definition: A protocol in which $n$ parties jointly generate a public key together with a threshold sharing of the matching secret key, so that no party ever holds the secret key and any authorized subset can use it.

newPages.title: Doubly-efficient RAM MPC
newPages.definition: An MPC protocol in the RAM model in which each party preprocesses its input offline once and can then run arbitrarily many executions whose online time is proportional only to the RAM running time of the program, which may be sublinear in the input size.

newPages.title: Garbled circuit
newPages.definition: A garbling scheme encodes a boolean circuit $C$ into a garbled circuit together with per-wire input labels, so that a party given the labels for an input $x$ can evaluate it to learn $C(x)$ and nothing further about $x$ or the intermediate wire values.

newPages.title: GKR protocol
newPages.definition: A public-coin interactive proof for any language computable by a log-space-uniform boolean circuit of depth $d$ on inputs of length $n$, with a polynomial-time prover, a verifier running in time $n \cdot \poly(d, \log n)$, and $\poly(d, \log n)$ communication.

newPages.title: Identification scheme
newPages.definition: A protocol in which a prover holding a secret key convinces a verifier holding the matching public key of its identity, canonically as a three-message commit-challenge-response sigma protocol such as Schnorr's proof of knowledge of a discrete logarithm.

newPages.title: Injective one-way function
newPages.definition: An injective one-way function is a one-way function that is injective but need not be length-preserving; MM11 shows that even a 1-bit-length-increasing injective OWF with adaptive one-wayness cannot be used to build a one-way permutation in a fully black-box way.

newPages.title: Language model watermarking
newPages.definition: A language model watermarking scheme embeds a hidden signal in a model's output that is detectable with a secret key, while remaining undetectable without it - watermarked text is computationally indistinguishable from the model's true output distribution.

newPages.title: Low-complexity pseudorandom generator
newPages.definition: A low-complexity PRG is a pseudorandom generator each of whose output bits is computable in NC^1 (and, for the NC^0 case, depends on a constant number of input bits); its existence is one of the four well-founded assumptions from which JLS21 builds indistinguishability obfuscation.

newPages.title: Merkle puzzles
newPages.definition: Merkle's Puzzles is a key-agreement protocol in the random oracle model in which the honest parties make O(n) oracle queries and any eavesdropper needs Omega(n^2) queries to recover the key - a quadratic, and by BM09 optimal, query gap.

newPages.title: Multi-prover interactive proofs
newPages.definition: MIP is the class of languages with an interactive proof in which a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier interacts with two or more computationally unbounded provers who cannot communicate with one another; MIP = NEXP.

newPages.title: Monotone span program
newPages.definition: A monotone span program over a field F is a matrix whose rows are labeled by parties together with a fixed target vector; a set of parties is authorized exactly when the target lies in the span of the rows they label - the linear-algebraic characterization of the access structures realizable by linear secret sharing.

newPages.title: Multilinear maps
newPages.definition: A cryptographic multilinear map generalizes a bilinear pairing to a k-way map e: G_1 x ... x G_k -> G_T that is linear in each argument and on which discrete-log-type problems are conjectured hard; the known candidates are graded encodings, and they underlie the first iO candidate (GGHRSW13).

newPages.title: Oblivious locally decodable code
newPages.definition: An oblivious locally decodable code is a secret-key locally decodable code in which the same party encodes the data and later decodes it locally, so that the physical access pattern of each local decoding hides which message position is being read.

newPages.title: Quantum money
newPages.definition: A quantum money scheme issues quantum states as banknotes that a holder of the verification key can check, while no efficient adversary can turn one valid banknote into two states that both verify.

newPages.title: Threshold encryption
newPages.definition: A threshold encryption scheme distributes the decryption key of a public-key encryption scheme among $n$ parties so that any $t$ of them can jointly decrypt a ciphertext, while any $t-1$ of them learn nothing about the plaintext.

newPages.title: Two-party differential privacy
newPages.definition: In two-party (distributed) differential privacy, two parties holding private datasets run a protocol computing a joint function of both datasets such that each party's view is differentially private with respect to the other party's dataset.

newPages.title: Unclonable encryption
newPages.definition: An unclonable encryption scheme encrypts a classical message into a quantum ciphertext that cannot be split between two parties in a way that lets both of them recover the message once the decryption key is later revealed.

newPages.title: Verifiable random function
newPages.definition: A verifiable random function is a keyed function whose secret-key holder outputs, for each input, the function value together with a proof that the value is correct with respect to a published public key, while values at unqueried inputs remain pseudorandom to anyone holding only the public key.
